Nextcloud Unauthenticated OS command injection in the richdocumentscode proxy
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: CVE-2026-110447, Summary: Users of Nextcloud with Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app can be vulnerable through proxy.php. A request can cause an operating system command to run as the web server user. The attack only works while the built-in CODE server is not running. So on a container restart, an upgrade, or after a crash. It is not sufficient to disable the app to avoid the problem, it must be upgraded to >= 26.4.303 or removed. Users of EOL Nextcloud <= 29 should upgrade their Nextcloud or remove this app. Standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected. This is not the same path as CVE-2025-66208, and the fix for that issue does not prevent it. Patches The bug was fixed in Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server (richdocumentscode) release 26.4.303. See also: https://github.com/CollaboraOnline/online/security/advisories/GHSA-g3vx-3m76-fghh

items.title: Apache CXF: Inoperative max_age authentication-freshness check in OidcClientCodeRequestFilter
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.1, CVEs: CVE-2026-71575, Summary: The max_age authentication-freshness check in OidcClientCodeRequestFilter was inoperative due to a milliseconds/seconds unit mismatch and an inverted comparison polarity. Any relying party using setMaxAgeOffset to enforce re-authentication would silently accept sessions of any age, bypassing step-up authentication policies. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

items.title: Authenticated RCE via MCP Stdio transport allows any user to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Proof-of-Concept, CVSSv3.1: 9.9, CVEs: CVE-2026-105740, Summary: Any authenticated Langflow user can achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by adding an MCP server with the "Stdio" transport. The user-supplied command field is passed directly to bash -c "exec {command}" with zero validation, no allowlisting, and no sandboxing. The command executes immediately when the server list is fetched. Additionally, the env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (e.g., LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). See also: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-105740, See also: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/langflows-critical-authenticated-rce.html

items.title: Russia Is Tightening Internet Controls, Leading to Operational Risks
items.summary: Since mid-2025, the Kremlin has intensified restrictions on digital communications and infrastructure, very likely to suppress the organization of domestic political dissent and conduct digital surveillance within Russia. Increasingly strict measures targeting virtual private networks (VPNs), state-managed internet shutdowns, limitations on civilian communications platforms, and monitoring of domestic and foreign entities very likely represent an escalation from the approaches to censorship and surveillance pursued prior to 2024. However, despite intensifying internet restrictions, technical and political limitations will likely prevent the Kremlin from achieving its long-held objective of a fully “sovereign internet” in the near term. The most likely scenario is that Moscow exerts extensive censorship and monitoring of online activity with increasingly strict –– though not absolute –– controls on circumvention and anonymizing tools. Insikt Group assesses that the Kremlin’s primary objectives regarding internet restrictions are twofold: facilitating extensive surveillance of online activity to support control over the domestic information space while maintaining connectivity to the global internet, and developing national internet infrastructure under Kremlin control, enabling isolation from the global internet if the Kremlin so chooses. Efforts in support of these objectives have almost certainly provided the Kremlin with enhanced ability to control and monitor domestic online discourse.

items.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
items.summary: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms.

items.title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories
items.summary: The credential-theft campaign known as GhostAction has ramped up, targeting more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations. The spike, according to GitGuardian, was observed on October 8 and 9, 2026. "This resulted from compromising the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users. It attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI," security researchers Gaetan Ferry and Guillaume Valadon said. GhostAction is the moniker for a supply chain attack campaign targeting developer infrastructure on GitHub. Originally discovered in September 2025, it involves threat actors compromising legitimate developer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions automation workflows into software repositories. "This payload was deployed in multiple phases," GitGuardian said. "First to 160 previously observed victims, then, 20 minutes later, to 28,000 new repositories between October 8 and 9. New waves have been observed, using the same payload, on October 10 and 12. However, GitHub started preventing the malicious workflow from running starting October 9. Those two subsequent waves therefore could not extract any secrets." Interestingly, a subset of the victims from this new burst were previously compromised in the September 2025 and August 2026 waves, indicating the threat actors are banking on unrotated secrets to pull them off.

items.title: Help TDS Linked to Hotejka as 20,000+ Cloudflare Pages Domains Host Tech Support Scams
items.summary: A long-running Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as Help TDS to a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, which appears to be a rebrand of a traffic monetization operation dubbed ROI777. Help TDS is assessed to be active since at least 2017, offering PHP code templates to partners and affiliates that are installed into compromised websites with an aim to direct unsuspecting users to tech support scams. These scams make use of full-screen browser manipulation and exit prevention techniques to serve bogus Microsoft Windows security alert screens instructing victims to contact a Windows Support number to address the problem. Since April 2026, the scams are run on free Cloudflare Pages sites (*.pages[.]dev), with the threat actor creating roughly 300 disposable pages per day. Over 20,000 such domains have been detected since then. In recent years, Hotejka has also been observed using different aliases on forums like CrackingX, seeking traffic from email spam and access to WordPress admin panels for prices starting at $100. In all, about 20 different affiliates, including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay, send traffic to Help TDS. These operations are known to heavily target WordPress sites to redirect victims to scams and malware.

Since April 2026, the scams are run on free Cloudflare Pages sites (*.pages[.]dev), with the threat actor creating roughly 300 disposable pages per day. Over 20,000 such domains have been detected since then. In recent years, Hotejka has also been observed using different aliases on forums like CrackingX, seeking traffic from email spam and access to WordPress admin panels for prices starting at $100.

In all, about 20 different affiliates, including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay, send traffic to Help TDS. These operations are known to heavily target WordPress sites to redirect victims to scams and malware.

items.title: Fake Calendar Invites Target Thousands of Organizations in Microsoft Credential-Phishing Campaign
items.summary: A calendar invite is one of the most routine messages in the modern workplace. It lands in the inbox, asks for a few seconds of attention, and is rarely questioned. Attackers know this, and they are now using fake meeting invitations to steal Microsoft account credentials. We have identified several large-scale phishing campaigns that abuse fake calendar invites to harvest credentials. Some arrive as an .ics attachment (example 1). The file is valid calendar data, so the attack abuses calendar features and user trust without exploiting a software vulnerability. Others use a link that appears to lead to a different destination (example 2). Both are designed to harvest the victim’s credentials. Check Point Email researchers are tracking these campaigns and have seen a significant surge starting September 25, 2026. A new detection layer specifically designed to identify this type of attack has flagged more than 302,386 unique phishing emails among our customers’ emails, sent to more than 40,000 organizations. The campaigns average more than 8,319 emails per active day. The emails came from more than 33,890 different sender domains and more than 247,270 unique sender addresses.

items.title: Ledger asks sellers across Asia to halt sales after supply-chain attack
items.summary: Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to halt wallet sales and remove products from shelves while it investigates hardware implant incidents. The company announced the decision in response to discovering that devices purchased from CryptoBilis had been modified to steal seed phrases used to access crypto assets and send them to an unauthorized party over an LTE connection. Ledger sells physical cryptocurrency wallets that securely store private keys used for managing and authorizing digital asset transactions. Following reports of cryptocurrency losses from multiple users, Ledger launched an investigation on October 9 and confirmed that some devices sold by CryptoBilis had been tampered with. Donjon said the implant’s microcontroller detects and decodes the 24-word recovery phrase for setting up and restoring the wallet, then transmits it over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component that does not modify the Secure Element or Ledger operating system, or alter transactions or signatures, which makes it undetectable by Ledger’s integrity self-checks.

items.title: UK Legal Aid Agency: Hackers stole records dating back to 1978
items.summary: The Legal Aid Agency (LAA), an executive agency of the UK's Ministry of Justice that manages the country's Public Defender Service, says attackers who breached its IT systems in April 2025 stole records dating back to 1978. The agency employs around 1,250 staff, oversees billions in legal funding, and works with approximately 2,000 providers, including barristers, solicitor firms, and non-profit organizations that deliver civil and criminal legal aid services in England and Wales. Two weeks later, it confirmed the resulting data breach was more serious than first believed after finding that attackers had stolen a large trove of sensitive applicant and recipient data from 2010 onward, including contact details, dates of birth, national ID numbers, criminal history, employment status, as well as contribution amounts, debts, and payments. After the LAA breach, which was followed by a string of cyberattacks targeting the Co-op, Harrods, and Marks & Spencer (M&S) UK retail chains ​​​claimed by the DragonForce ransomware operation, the country's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) published guidance and advised UK organizations to follow it to strengthen their cybersecurity defenses.

items.title: Hackers hijack D-Link, Ubiquiti devices to resell your stolen bandwidth
items.summary: A proxyjacking campaign has impacted devices in 34 countries, monetizing victims’ internet connections through a commercial residential proxy network. The operator installed Pawns.app, a legitimate bandwidth-sharing application that lets users earn money by sharing their internet connections, on devices without the owners’ consent. Pawns.app account holders are rewarded for allowing traffic from other users to flow through their network, provided it runs on trusted, non-blocking IP addresses. Threat intelligence company GreyNoise discovered the campaign while investigating suspicious activity at an unnamed organization, and identified at least 143 compromised devices worldwide.

items.title: Fake Arch Linux packages push malware with root privileges
items.summary: A threat actor uploaded malicious packages to the Arch User Repository (AUR) that impersonated two popular helper tools, yay and paru. AUR is a community-maintained, widely-used package index for Arch Linux and derivative distributions that hosts package build scripts (PKGBUILDs) for third-party and proprietary tools, beta, or older package versions that are no longer available via the official Linux distribution channels. The repository has recently become a target of malicious campaigns, including an attack in June in which 400 packages distributed credential-stealing malware with rootkit capabilities. Another campaign in July prompted Arch to temporarily disable package adoption. The latest campaign was detected on October 13 and involved malicious packages uploaded by a user named “marchos1as” under typosquatted names mimicking the yay and paru command-line tools. Also known as AUR helpers, these tools simplify software management on Arch Linux by streamlining the retrieval and installation of user-contributed packages.

items.title: NGINX Fixes 5 Flaws, Including Possible RCE and a TLS Bug That May Skip Client-Cert Checks
items.summary: NGINX released versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 on October 14 to fix five vulnerabilities, one of them present in every release since May 2005. There are three memory bugs that F5, the company behind NGINX, says could crash a worker process or possibly let an attacker run code, and each requires a specific configuration to exploit. A fourth lets an attacker forge a TLS session that could get past client-certificate checks, though F5 calls the forgery non-deterministic and beyond the attacker's control. The fifth lets an HTTP/3 client slip extra bytes into a request that NGINX passes on to a backend. None of the five was in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of October 15, and neither NGINX nor F5 reports attacks. NGINX rates all five medium. F5 scores the three memory bugs 9.2, Critical, on CVSS v4.0, the TLS flaw 8.3, and the HTTP/3 flaw 6.9.

items.title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules
items.summary: Drupal core has a critical flaw in its Field UI module that could let an attacker run code on the site's server, and fixes were shipped on October 14 in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19. An attacker cannot reach the flaw through core alone, the Drupal Security Team said in its advisory. Several exploit paths exist through contributed modules, and at least one known path needs no login. Tracked as CVE-2026-108097, the flaw sits in Field UI, the core module behind the admin pages where site builders manage fields and how they display. Drupal rates it 19 out of 25 on its own risk scale, the level the project calls critical.

items.title: Hackers exploit Collabora RCE flaw to backdoor Nextcloud servers
items.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical command execution flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-110447, in the Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) for Nextcloud. Multiple administrator reports indicate that attacks began in mid-September, roughly a month before the formal security bulletin, the GitHub advisory, and CVE publication. CVE-2026-110447 impacts richdocumentscode versions before 26.4.303 and resides in the Nextcloud app’s mechanism for starting the bundled Collabora server.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls. The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices. Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks. "Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said. To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface. Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only. The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.

items.title: Unit 42 Uncovers PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
items.summary: Unit 42 investigated a multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization that occurred in September 2024, which we are tracking as cluster CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820). The attackers behind CL-STA-0954 achieved an initial compromise by exploiting CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance. From that single appliance, our observations are that the attackers exfiltrated an archive containing running configurations, cryptographic material and database files containing information about more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Those firewalls protected the target's own infrastructure and the networks of its clients. The discovery of the PEERSTITCH implant demonstrates the increasing technical maturity of edge-device malware. By operating as a one-shot injector, avoiding persistent disk artifacts and building a covert inter-process communication bridge inside process memory, the attackers achieved sustained persistence while evading traditional monitoring. For organizations that manage infrastructure on behalf of others, the management platform is the highest-value target on the network. Compromising the management platform is not contained by the boundary of the organization that owns it. That compromise also does not end when the platform is patched.

items.title: Asiantuntija järkyttyi – tietävätkö ihmiset, mitä he nyt asentavat laitteelleen?
items.summary: Metan syyskuun alussa julkaisema tekoälyagentti Muse kohosi nopeasti sovelluslatausten kärkeen Yhdysvalloissa, ja miljoonat ovat ottaneet sen käyttöönsä. Time-lehden mukaan Muse kerää harvinaisen hanakasti käyttäjiensä ja myös muiden ihmisten tietoja. Muse toimii omana sovelluksenaan tai Metan WhatsApp-, Messenger- ja Instagram-sovellusten sisällä. Palvelu ei ole ainakaan toistaiseksi käytössä EU:ssa. Time tarkasteli Musen sisäistä ohjeistusta, joka olisi kaikkien luettavissa. Muse rakentaa käyttäjistään jatkuvasti päivittyviä kansioita keskittyen siihen, ketkä ovat käyttäjälle tärkeitä, mitä käyttäjät himoitsevat ja miten heidän käytöstään voitaisiin hienovaraisesti ohjata. Walsh kuvailee Musea kaupalliseksi vakoiluverkostoksi, joka on naamioitu käyttäjän henkilökohtaiseksi avustajaksi. Asiantuntija painottaa, että Musella on pääsy muun muassa yksityisiin viesteihin, sähköposteihin, pankkitileihin, yhteystietoihin ja henkilökohtaiseen tietoon. Muse ei ole toistaiseksi saatavilla Euroopan unionissa. On epäselvää, miten Metan pitäisi mahdollisesti muuttaa Musea, jotta se noudattaisi EU:n tietosuojalainsäädäntöä. EU:n gdpr-asetus ja digimarkkinasäädös asettavat yrityksille tiukat vaatimukset tietosuojasta ja eri palveluiden tietojen yhdistelemisestä.
